title: Prosecuting Financial Crime: Evidence, Experts and the Courtroom
summary: An eight-module programme equipping prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases, from charge and evidence to sentencing and confiscation.
intro: This training programme equips prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases with confidence, from proving knowledge and presenting financial evidence to managing experts, disclosure, sentencing and confiscation.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give prosecutors and judges a practical understanding of how financial crime cases are built, proved and tried, and of the evidential issues that most often cause them to fail. Participants leave able to frame charges, assess complex financial evidence and expert testimony, manage disclosure and case management fairly, and secure effective sentencing and confiscation outcomes.
sections.What It Covers: Money laundering offences and the international standards, charging decisions and case strategy, proving criminal property and knowledge, complex financial and digital evidence, expert witnesses, disclosure and case management, sentencing, confiscation and ancillary orders, and mutual legal assistance and cross-border evidence.
Intended Audience: Prosecutors handling money laundering, fraud, corruption and other economic crime
Judges and magistrates hearing financial crime, restraint and confiscation cases
Senior investigators and legal advisers who prepare financial crime cases for prosecution
Learning Objectives: Explain the elements of money laundering offences and the standards that shape them
Assess the evidence needed to prove criminal property and the required mental element
Evaluate complex financial and digital evidence and the reliability of expert testimony
Apply disclosure and case management principles to large financial cases
Secure proportionate sentences and effective confiscation orders
Use mutual legal assistance to obtain evidence and recover assets abroad
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a legal and technical briefing with case studies and evidential exercises, ending in a mock hearing workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the legal system and the participants' roles.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of criminal prosecution, judicial work or financial crime investigation is helpful. No accounting or technical background is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
UNODC (2012), Manual on Mutual Legal Assistance and Extradition
World Bank and UNODC StAR Initiative (2021), Asset Recovery Handbook: A Guide for Practitioners, Second Edition

modules.title: Money Laundering Offences and International Standards
modules.summary: The elements of money laundering offences, the range of predicate offences, and the international standards that shape national offences and expectations of effective prosecution.
objectives: Explain the physical and mental elements of money laundering offences
Summarise the expectations of FATF Recommendation 3 and Immediate Outcome 7
Distinguish the main types of money laundering prosecution
syllabus: Concealment, acquisition, possession and use of criminal property
All-crimes and listed-offence approaches to predicate offences
Self-laundering, third-party laundering and stand-alone cases
FATF Recommendation 3, Immediate Outcome 7 and common weaknesses

modules.title: Charging Decisions and Case Strategy
modules.summary: How prosecutors decide whether and what to charge in financial crime cases, work with investigators from an early stage and build a case theory the evidence can sustain.
objectives: Apply evidential and public interest tests to financial crime cases
Select charges that reflect the criminality and can be proved
Shape investigations through early prosecutorial advice
syllabus: Early prosecutorial involvement and investigative advice
Choosing charges: predicate, laundering, conspiracy and corporate liability
Case theory, indictment design and keeping cases manageable
Alternatives: negotiated outcomes, deferred prosecution and non-trial resolution

modules.title: Proving Criminal Property and Knowledge
modules.summary: How to prove that property derives from crime and that the defendant knew or suspected it, including through circumstantial evidence and inference where the predicate offence cannot be identified.
objectives: Explain how criminal origin can be proved without a conviction for the predicate offence
Assess circumstantial evidence of knowledge, suspicion and wilful blindness
Anticipate common defences and how to address them
syllabus: Proving criminal origin by inference from the circumstances
Knowledge, suspicion, recklessness and wilful blindness
Indicators from conduct, lifestyle and transaction patterns
Common defences: legitimate business, ignorance and reliance on others

modules.title: Complex Financial and Digital Evidence
modules.summary: How to understand, test and present large volumes of financial and digital evidence, from bank records and corporate documents to communications data and blockchain analysis.
objectives: Assess the admissibility, reliability and continuity of financial evidence
Scrutinise schedules, charts and summaries prepared by investigators
Evaluate digital and blockchain evidence critically
syllabus: Bank, corporate and accounting records as evidence
Schedules, charts and summaries: accuracy and fairness
Electronic and communications evidence and continuity
Blockchain tracing outputs and their evidential limits

modules.title: Expert Witnesses in Financial Cases
modules.summary: When expert evidence is needed in financial cases, how to instruct and test experts, the duties experts owe the court, and how judges manage conflicting expert opinion.
objectives: Identify issues that require expert rather than factual evidence
Instruct experts with clear questions and appropriate material
Test expert methodology, independence and the limits of opinion
syllabus: Forensic accountants, market specialists and blockchain analysts
Letters of instruction, independence and the expert's duty to the court
Testing methodology, assumptions and conclusions
Managing competing experts and joint statements

modules.title: Disclosure and Case Management in Large Cases
modules.summary: How to meet disclosure obligations fairly in document-heavy financial cases, use technology to manage material, and keep complex trials on track through active case management.
objectives: Apply disclosure duties to large volumes of material
Use technology-assisted review defensibly
Manage complex cases actively from first hearing to trial
syllabus: Disclosure principles: relevance and material that undermines or assists
Search terms, technology-assisted review and audit trails
Third-party, foreign and sensitive material
Case management hearings, timetables and narrowing the issues

modules.title: Sentencing, Confiscation and Ancillary Orders
modules.summary: How courts approach sentencing in money laundering and financial crime cases, the link with confiscation proceedings, and the ancillary orders that disrupt future offending.
objectives: Apply sentencing factors to money laundering and economic crime
Explain benefit, the available amount and enforcement of confiscation
Use ancillary orders to prevent further offending
syllabus: Sentencing factors: culpability, harm, role and sums laundered
Confiscation: benefit, extended confiscation and the available amount
Enforcement of confiscation orders and default terms
Ancillary orders: disqualification, prevention orders and compensation

modules.title: Cross-Border Cases and Mock Hearing Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining mutual legal assistance and foreign evidence, ending with a mock hearing in which participants argue and decide the key issues in a laundering case.
objectives: Draft effective mutual legal assistance requests for evidence and assets
Manage the admissibility and use of evidence obtained abroad
Apply the programme to argue and decide a realistic case
syllabus: Mutual legal assistance: dual criminality, content and timing
Joint investigation teams and direct cooperation between prosecutors
Admissibility and use of foreign evidence
Workshop: mock hearing on knowledge, evidence and confiscation

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.

related.title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.

related.title: Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime Investigations
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud, money mules and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to recover funds.

related.title: Public-Private Partnerships and Financial Intelligence Sharing
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping FIUs and law-enforcement agencies to design, run and evaluate public-private partnerships for sharing financial intelligence lawfully and effectively.

related.title: Tax Crime and Money Laundering
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping tax, FIU and law-enforcement investigators to tackle tax crime and related laundering through information exchange and joint investigation.
